description: Bounds of the one acceptance test every single-unit retry of this pipeline passes through: the echo retry, the term ladder's pinned retranslation, and the short unit top-up. The upstream translator already refuses a paragraph reply whose token count leaves 0.3..3 of its input; the passes this project added asked their own narrower questions -- does the reply parse, does it differ from the source, does the ruled rendering appear in it -- and none of them asked how big the answer was, which is how four sentences of invented copy about a courier company reached a footer under the ruled string ERNCOURIER. Size is measured in units comparable across scripts -- one Han character or one run of letters or digits in any other script counts as one -- because characters cannot be compared across this corpus's two directions: measured in characters, the widest honest zh->en expansion in the B18 corpus runs 6.79 out per one in while a reply that must be refused runs 15.5, and two thresholds that close cannot both be safe. Measured this way the whole corpus of 1456 translated units sits at or under 9.0 and the two refused replies sit at 7.75 and 118. retry_sentence_max_ratio is the first test: a unit carrying no sentence-terminal punctuation is a name, a label or a fragment, and an answer that comes back as a sentence several times its size is prose about the unit rather than the unit. Five clears every honest fragment translation in the corpus, the widest of which runs 3.69, and catches both refused replies. retry_output_max_ratio and retry_output_max_chars are the gross-length backstop and both have to be exceeded before a reply is refused: a ratio alone would refuse an honest expansion and a cap alone would refuse the long paragraph a term retry may legitimately be handed. A refused reply changes nothing: the caller keeps the source byte for byte, records the typed reason, does not ask again, and discards the reply from the translation cache so the next run asks rather than being handed what this one refused.
